title: Keryx portable bundle manifest
description: planned — Declares the manifest shape at the root of a bundle produced by `keryx bundle export` and consumed by `keryx bundle import|inspect|verify` (W4). No runtime reads or writes this shape yet; it is the target contract for moving skills, rules, agent definitions, learned patterns, memory entries, and hook configs between project/team/user scopes and across harnesses, described in workstreams/W4-portability.md.

formatVersion.description: Semver of the bundle format itself, distinct from `sourceKeryxVersion`. A consumer must fail closed on a `formatVersion` whose major it does not recognise rather than guess at an unknown shape.

bundleId.description: Stable identifier for this bundle across re-exports. A content edit produces a new `contents[].sha256` but the same `bundleId`, so `keryx bundle inspect` can report 'this is bundle X, contents changed' instead of treating every export as unrelated.

createdAt.description: When `keryx bundle export` produced this bundle.

sourceKeryxVersion.description: The exporting Keryx build's own version string, for compatibility diagnostics distinct from `formatVersion`.

contents.description: One entry per file this bundle carries. `bundle import` verifies every entry's `sha256` before writing anything (fail closed on any mismatch, W4-AC3).

scope.description: Which scope this entry targets on apply. `team` is a labeling and transfer discipline over the same project-scope tree, not a separate on-disk root (see workstreams/W4-portability.md, 'Scopes'). `user` targets the `~/.keryx/` root.

contentKind.description: What kind of catalog content this entry carries. `agent` entries validate against agent-definition.schema.json (W2); `learned-pattern` entries validate against learned-pattern.schema.json (W3); `hook-config` entries validate against hook-config.schema.json (W6). This schema constrains only the envelope, not those sibling schemas' internal shape.

harnessId.description: Matches the harness ids used by the unified adapter registry (W5). `keryx-shell` denotes Keryx's own agent shell rather than a host harness.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 digest of the entry's exact bytes as stored in the bundle, following the sha256 content-addressing pattern already used elsewhere in Keryx (e.g. src/assets/resolver.ts, src/harness/run/run.ts canonical-JSON fingerprints) rather than a new hashing scheme.

producedBy.description: Fixed marker distinguishing a genuine export from a hand-assembled directory masquerading as one.

sourceProject.description: Never a raw absolute path (a bundle shared outside the originating machine must not leak that path). Either omitted, or a hash of a normalized project identifier.

sourceScope.description: The scope this bundle was exported from.

minKeryxVersion.description: Lowest Keryx version expected to understand every content kind present in `contents`.

targetHarnesses.description: Advisory hint only, never a hard gate: harnesses the bundle's author believes its hook-config/rule entries suit. `keryx bundle inspect` warns when a named harness is not `native`/`adapter` in the importing project's W5 capability matrix, but the source of truth for what actually works is that matrix, not this field.

path.description: Path relative to the bundle root, mirroring the on-disk layout this entry's `kind` and `scope` target (e.g. a user-scope skill: `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, matching `~/.keryx/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), so apply is a direct copy rather than a kind-specific rewrite.

description.description: Optional human-readable one-liner shown in `keryx bundle inspect` output.

external.description: True when this entry is referenced (not copied) from an externally-authored Agent-Skills-standard-conformant catalog, per the import path in workstreams/W4-portability.md. False or absent means the content is Keryx-authored/generated/learned and is carried inline in the bundle.

sourceRef.description: For an `external: true` entry, a pointer to the original catalog location (URL, path, or catalog id) the content is referenced from, so a later `verify`/`inspect` can report an unresolvable reference distinctly from a checksum mismatch.
